newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese parliament starts budget debate.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese parliament starts budget debate.

text.p: The Lebanese parliament started on Wednesday its debate of the 1997 state budget.
The debate is expected to last until Saturday, with at least 30 MPs in the 128-member parliament having asked to speak.
The original budget draft approved by the government last September proposed expenditures of 6,400 billion Lebanese pounds against income of 4,100 billion.

But the government approved on Saturday a 233 billion Lebanese pounds increase in proposed budget spending and decided to offset it by cutting subsidies to electricity consumers by 200 billion pounds.

The net increase of 33 billion pounds ($21 million) raised spending by 0.5 percent and widened the deficit of planned income against expenditure to about 37.5 percent, Information Minister Bassem al-Sabaa has told reporters.
The size of the proposed deficit is expected to be a major issue during the parliamentary budget debate.
The 1996 deficit, planned as 2,428 billion pounds or 38 percent of expenditure, in fact ended up at 3,692 billion pounds or 51 percent.
